record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: When a feedback controller operates in the continuous-actuation limit, meaning that it repeatedly acts on the system with a period shorter than every characteristic time scale of the system dynamics, how can results for correlated repeated feedback actuation be extended to that limit despite the nontrivial relationship between differential entropy and discrete entropy?

evidence.quote: the controller repeatedly actuates on the system with a period shorter than any of the characteristic time scales of the system dynamics
the continuous time limit of the results found in [13] is not direct because of the nontrivial relationship between differential entropy and discrete entropy
Therefore, even the extension of the results in [13] to the continuous actuation limit remains still an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic dynamical system whose state $X_t$ evolves under the action of a feedback controller. At a sequence of discrete times $t_k = k\tau$ ($k=0,1,2,\dots$) the controller performs measurements $Y_k$ of the state and applies actuations based on the (correlated) history of those measurements. For the discrete-time setting one has thermodynamic and information-theoretic identities (e.g., generalized second-law inequalities and bounds on extractable work) expressed in terms of the discrete Shannon mutual information $I(X_{t_k};Y_k)$ accumulated over the sequence of correlated repeated feedback actuations, and in terms of discrete Shannon entropies of the measurement records.

Problem. Formulate and prove an extension of these results to the continuous-actuation limit, defined as $\tau \to 0$ with the feedback period $\tau$ shorter than every characteristic time scale of the system dynamics. Specifically, derive the appropriate continuous-time analogues of the discrete information-theoretic bounds in this limit, accounting rigorously for the nontrivial relationship between discrete Shannon entropy and differential entropy (the latter generally diverging as the measurement resolution becomes continuous), so that the limiting bounds are finite, well-defined, and reduce to the discrete results for finite $\tau$.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution was located. The problem of extending discrete-time correlated-feedback information-thermodynamic results to the continuous-actuation limit, while properly handling the gap between differential and discrete entropy, appears to remain a recognized open direction in stochastic thermodynamics with feedback; no clear published solution was found.
